evals.name: tenant-from-not-filter
evals.prompt: A Screenplay query `ListInvoices => InvoiceListReadModel[]` declares `filter tenantId TenantId` so the UI sends the tenant. Review the security of this and show the corrected query. Give the code in your reply; do not write files. Separately, Screenplay 6.32.0 reports PLAY0273 for DispatchSummary.detail typed as another readmodel DispatchDetail. Show the reusable-value extraction. For OpenDispatches => observable DispatchSummary[] with a C# performer, explain context/result versions, readModels, snapshots, subscription disposal and frozen context. Do not infer that Stage 4.197.0 implements this contract; what about observable optional results?
evals.expected_output: Anything the caller must not choose belongs on a `from` parameter, not a caller-supplied `filter`: `filter tenantId TenantId from $context.tenant`. The `from` states the contract and the runtime enforces it; a compiling query is not evidence that access control works, so pin denial with `given caller` and `then denied`. Extract DispatchDetail's fields into a top-level type DispatchDetailValue and use it as DispatchSummary.detail; members admit primitives, concepts and top-level reusable types, not read-model identities or slice-local types (4.256.0, PLAY0273). Live collection performers carry ContextVersion 1/ResultVersion 2: host-defined LiveReadModels<T> is only IObservable<IEnumerable<T>>, initial/current and then complete snapshots, not deltas or guaranteed changes. Read only declared T; one subscription per client, dispose on unsubscribe/disconnect/shutdown; OnError/OnCompleted end it without resubscription. Context is captured once, ReceivedAt stays fixed, no cancellation member. Optional/single live results have no live contract; this 4.256.0 Screenplay binding does not establish Stage runtime support.
assertions: Says a caller-chosen `filter` for the tenant is a security flaw because the caller must not choose it.
Uses a `from` source such as `filter tenantId TenantId from $context.tenant`.
States that a compiling query is not evidence that access control works, since the runtime enforces the `from`.
Recommends a specification with `given caller` including a `then denied` case for an authorized query.

Repairs PLAY0273 through a top-level value type and accurately describes the live collection v1/v2 contract, complete snapshots, declared reads, fixed context and disposal without inventing optional/single live or Stage support.

evals.name: scoped-to-global
evals.prompt: In review we find `query Everyones => Timesheet[]` with `scoped to global`. A teammate says it is harmless metadata. What does it do, what is the default, and how should a reviewer treat it? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A query is scoped to the tenant it runs for by default and that stays unstated; `scoped to global` opts out and reaches past the tenant. The dangerous case is the one you have to write down. Scope is a name, not a closed set (`identity` and `global` are documented), and a query declares at most one. Every `scoped to global` is a question to answer in review.
assertions: Says the tenant is the default scope and stays unstated.
Says `scoped to global` opts out of tenant scoping and reaches past the tenant.
Treats each `scoped to global` as a question the reviewer must answer, not a detail.
States that a query declares at most one scope and the scope is a name, not a closed set.

evals.name: no-invented-paging
evals.prompt: Add paging (20 per page) and sorting by name to `query ListBoats => BoatReadModel[]` in our Screenplay model, and make it update live when boats change. What syntax do you write? Give the code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Paging, sorting and change-set delivery are planned but not in the language yet, so do not invent syntax. Liveness is declared with `observable` before the result type: `=> observable BoatReadModel[]`, which composes with `[]`, filters and `authorize`; without it the query is one-shot.
assertions: Declines to invent paging or sorting syntax and says they are not in the language yet.
Writes `observable` in the return type, for example `=> observable BoatReadModel[]`.
States that without the marker a query is one-shot.
Notes that the delivery of a live result is the target runtime's concern.

evals.name: ambiguous-references
evals.prompt: Two slices in our model each declare `query All`. A screen says `data QueueReadModel[] via query All` and another navigates to `OrdersScreen`, which was renamed. CI is green. Why, and what do we change? Also, a colleague wrote `query GetBoat => BoatRM optional by id BoatId` on one line; is that valid? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Unresolved and ambiguous references are warnings, not errors, because a name may resolve outside the document. Run with `--warnaserror`. Qualify the name with any trailing part of the scope (`Queue.All`) using the shortest unambiguous form. The key goes on its own `by` line in the body; `by` on the header line is a declaration error.
assertions: Says unresolved and ambiguous references are warnings, not errors, so the build stays green.
Recommends running with `--warnaserror`.
Qualifies the ambiguous query with a trailing scope part such as `Queue.All`, using the shortest unambiguous form.
Says `by id BoatId` on the query header line is a declaration error and belongs on its own `by` line in the body.

evals.name: named-sink-and-sink-property
evals.prompt: Our Screenplay model has `readmodel CustomerRevenue` (customerId CustomerId key, total Money) built by a projection, and reporting read models must live in a separate reporting database. Another read model, `Dispatch`, already has a line `sink Warehouse` where `Warehouse` is a concept. Store CustomerRevenue in the reporting store and tell me whether the Dispatch line changes meaning. Show the .play changes in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Declares `sink Reporting for readmodels` once at the application root and adds a bare `sink Reporting` line to the CustomerRevenue body, without naming a database, engine or connection in the model and without naming a sink on the projection or query. Explains that `sink Warehouse` in Dispatch stays a property named `sink` of type `Warehouse`, because no sink called `Warehouse` is declared, and that `@sink <Type>` always means the property.
assertions: Declares the sink once at the application root as `sink Reporting for readmodels` (any name), not inside a module or read model.
Adds a bare `sink <Name>` line to the CustomerRevenue read model body and names no sink on the projection or the query.
Names no database, engine, connection string or server in the model; says the deployment maps the sink name to storage.
Says `sink Warehouse` in Dispatch stays a property named `sink` of type `Warehouse` because no sink called `Warehouse` is declared.
Mentions that `@sink <Type>` always declares the property, or that a `passive` read model cannot name a sink (PLAY0935).
